text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Twenty people assassinated in Benkhelil in the province of Blida.
- Rules adapted to ensure political plurality. Story refers to laws shaping political parties.
- Government adopts draft law on political parties and opts for proportional representation to elect popular assemblies.
- Washington confirms arrest of Islamic Salvation Front spokesman Anwar Haddam.
- Presidency gives the go-ahead for bilateral meetings, as follow-up to constitutional referendum, starting next week.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia rejects conditions of university strikers.
- Horror at dawn: Islamists kill passengers of a bus near Boufarik at 3 a.m.
- The United States immigration services arrests FIS spokesman abroad Anwar Haddam after he was found in irregular situation.
- Again, carnage in Blida with 23 killed and 10 wounded.
- Former customs workers' union secretary general in detention.
- While French judge carries out investigation in Italy over "terrorist" acts, France's authorities free 14 Islamists.
